LATIN TIMES: Cartel Drones Carrying Explosives Mark New Concern Near Texas Border
July 1, 2026 | 🔴

📰 A "new concern" that recycles drone-fear reporting already circulating since February. The one documented cartel drone bombing this cycle hit a state prosecutor's office in Tijuana — a Mexican target, inside Mexico. 🔍

Framed as a menace creeping toward Texas; the actual victims of cartel drones have been Mexican police and communities, not the US border.

BLOOMBERG: Nissan Cuts Costs on Mexico-Made Cars to Mitigate 25% Tariffs
July 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Nissan is slashing costs on its Mexico-built cars to survive Trump's 25% tariff. The framing treats Mexican production as the liability — but Nissan itself says the entry-level Sentra and Kicks can't be built affordably in the US. 🇲🇽

The tariff doesn't punish Mexico so much as US buyers: it's the reason a $22,600 Sentra gets more expensive on American lots.

WASHINGTON POST: Fate of $2 Trillion North American Trade Deal in Doubt as July 1 Deadline Passes
July 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The headline says the deal is "in doubt." What actually passed the deadline is Trump declining to extend USMCA — while Mexico offered a 16-year renewal and kept negotiating. Canada, per the piece, stayed "disengaged." 🔍

The "doubt" is US-made: absent a deal, the pact just runs annual reviews toward a 2036 expiry. Mexico showed up; Washington chose the slow wind-down.

REUTERS/AOL: US Imposes Sanctions on Mexicans Tied to Fuel Smuggling Network
July 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 US Treasury sanctions two Mexicans and nine firms over CJNG fuel smuggling. Buried in the release: the fuel is smuggled FROM the US, and Treasury admits "complicit U.S. companies" laundered the profits into luxury goods and real estate. 🇲🇽

The scheme only works because US refiners sell the fuel and US shell companies wash the money — a binational operation headlined as a Mexican one.

• "Today's action highlights the extent to which Mexico's cartels are expanding beyond traditional drug trafficking"
• "Complicit U.S. companies… leverage their relationships with major refineries and fuel distributors"

🇲🇽📊 MEXICO'S BOOKS ARE BEATING THE FORECASTS

Hacienda's numbers through May: a primary surplus of 15 billion pesos where a 165-billion-peso deficit was projected, public debt down to 47.4% of GDP from 49.2% a year earlier, and debt-servicing costs falling 9.6% in real terms — 86 billion pesos below plan, helped by a strong peso.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 MEXICO SENDS POWER PLANTS AND A NAVY SHIP TO VENEZUELA

After earthquakes that have killed more than 1,700 people, Sheinbaum is flying seven electricity-generating plants to Venezuela and loading a Marina ship with food and supplies — on top of the 250-plus Mexican rescuers already on the ground. "They're a pride of Mexico," she said of the teams.

🔥🇲🇽 THE ABC DAYCARE CASE IS REOPENED — 49 BABIES, 17 YEARS ON

Sheinbaum says the FGR "must go to the last consequences" on the 2009 ABC daycare fire that killed 49 infants and injured 104. After the Supreme Court ruled that grave human rights violations never expire, the case is back open — the daycare had been running under an IMSS subrogation contract stripped of safety standards in the privatization years.

🇲🇽🚆 MEXICO IS BUILDING BACK 3,000 KM OF PASSENGER RAIL

The government just published its 2026–2030 rail program: 13 new lines, more than 3,000 km of passenger track, reaching over 49 million people — AIFA–Pachuca, Mexico City–Querétaro, Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo and more. Passenger trains were gutted under neoliberal privatization in the 1990s; a state agency is laying the track again.

🔥🇲🇽 THEY SOLD TEACHING JOBS AND KEPT THE PAYCHECKS

Ten State of Mexico officials are now in pretrial detention for a payroll scam running since 2021: 168 ghost teachers registered through 324 fake payroll movements, each handed a debit card paying 2,000–4,000 pesos a fortnight — then the ring kept the cards, skimming around 10 million pesos a month off the state education budget.

🇲🇽🏭 FOREIGN INVESTMENT HITS RECORD $23.6 BILLION IN MEXICO

Mexico drew a record 23,591 million dollars in foreign direct investment in Q1 2026 — up 10.4% year-on-year and the strongest first quarter ever, per El Financiero on Economy Ministry data. 94.2% ($22.2B) was profit reinvestment: companies already operating here doubling down. The US led with $10.2B, Spain $3.8B.
